answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph: each step follows verified attestations, while transition mass is constrained by conductance. A Sybil cluster gains influence only through its boundary; if its external cut is sparse, low conductance traps walk mass internally. Cheeger-style bounds limit escape and, through min-cut transitivity, cap the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, so a fable at the wharf cannot bridge honest consensus.
